name: Spatial Pin/Hotspot (Tap on Image)

tier.label: Apply — Using Information in New Contexts

summary: Tap a specific location on an image (map, diagram, photo). Validated against a correct zone with proximity-based partial credit.

aiGenerability.notes: AI can generate questions and define correct zones, but requires pre-existing reference images with coordinate mappings. Works well with standard educational images (maps, anatomy, architecture, etc.).

prompt.description: Question asking learner to tap a specific location on the image. Must be clear and unambiguous.

imageUrl.description: URL to the reference image. Must be a real, accessible image (map, diagram, photo, chart).

imageAlt.description: Descriptive alt text for the image (accessibility).

correctZone.description: Defines the correct area on the image as a center point and radius.

x.description: X coordinate (pixels) of the center of the correct zone, relative to image.

y.description: Y coordinate (pixels) of the center of the correct zone, relative to image.

radius.description: Radius (pixels) of the acceptable zone around the center. Learner can tap anywhere within this radius.

explanation.description: Explanation of the correct location and its context.

distractorHints.description: Optional common wrong answers to address in explanation (e.g., 'Not Cairo, which is further north').

ux.mobileNotes: Image is responsive, zoomed to fit mobile screen. After tap, a pin appears at the tap location with visual feedback (glow or pulse). On correct answer, show a green pin at correct location. On incorrect, show both learner's pin (red) and correct pin (green).

ageAdaptations.8-10: Simple maps or diagrams with large regions. Larger acceptable zones (radius: 40–60px). Questions about familiar locations (continents, oceans, planets). After incorrect tap, show visual outline of correct region.
ageAdaptations.11-13: More detailed maps (countries, states, major cities) or anatomy diagrams (organs, body systems). Moderate zones (radius: 25–40px). Questions require moderate geographic or anatomical knowledge. Feedback shows distance from correct location.
ageAdaptations.14-16: Detailed maps (small cities, provinces) or precise diagrams (cell structures, architectural plans). Tight zones (radius: 10–25px). Questions demand precise knowledge or map-reading skills. No visual hints; learner must know exact location.
